<script>
  // Restore the saved color scheme preference, or
  // enact the browser preference if "automatic", 
  // without expecting DOM load to have completed.
  //
  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);
    }
    // Pre-apply spinout-banner dismissal here, before the banner paints, so it
    // never flashes in only to be hidden later by the deferred arxiv-header.js.
    // Key matches arxiv-header.js: "arxiv-banner-dismissed:" + data-banner-name.
    if (localStorage.getItem('arxiv-banner-dismissed:spinout-nonprofit')) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-banner-dismissed", "");
    }
  }
  // Run as soon as JS starts, to minimize repainting
  initializeReadingPreferences();
</script>

<article class="ltx_document">
<h1 class="ltx_title ltx_title_document">FLARE: Fast Low-rank Attention Routing Engine</h1>
<div class="ltx_authors">
<span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Vedant Puri

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p">The quadratic complexity of self-attention limits the scalability of transformers on long sequences.
We introduce <em id="abstract1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Fast Low-rank Attention Routing Engine (FLARE)</em>, a token-mixing operator that realizes low-rank attention by routing information through a small set of latent tokens.
Each layer induces an input-input token mixing matrix of rank at most <math id="abstract1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> via a minimal encode-decode factorization implemented using only two standard scaled dot-product attention (SDPA) calls.
Because the dominant <math id="abstract1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}(NM)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}(NM)</annotation></semantics></math> computation is expressed purely in terms of standard SDPA, FLARE is compatible with fused attention kernels and avoids materializing <math id="abstract1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M\times N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M\times N</annotation></semantics></math> projection matrices.
FLARE further assigns disjoint latent slices to each attention head, yielding a mixture of head-specific low-rank pathways.
Empirically, FLARE scales to <em id="abstract1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">one-million-point</em> unstructured meshes on a single GPU, achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on PDE surrogate benchmarks, and outperforms general-purpose efficient-attention methods on the Long Range Arena suite.
We additionally release a large-scale additive manufacturing benchmark dataset.
Our code is available at <a href="https://github.com/vpuri3/FLARE.py" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://github.com/vpuri3/FLARE.py</a></p>
  
</div>
<div class="ltx_keywords">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_keywords">Keywords: </h6>Machine Learning, ICML
</div>
<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1 </span>Introduction</h2>

<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">High-fidelity simulations of physical systems are often too costly for multi-query applications such as design optimization and uncertainty quantification.
Neural surrogate models offer a promising alternative by learning mappings from simulation inputs to outputs, enabling rapid evaluation once trained.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Transformers <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">Vaswani et al., 2017</a>)</cite> have demonstrated strong scalability and generalization across domains including natural language processing <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Devlin et al., 2019</a>)</cite> and computer vision <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Dosovitskiy et al., 2020</a>)</cite>.
This success has motivated their adoption for spatially distributed scientific data such as point clouds and unstructured meshes, where each mesh point is treated as a token with geometric and physical features.
However, standard self-attention scales as <math id="S1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}(N^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>N</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}(N^{2})</annotation></semantics></math> in both time and memory for <math id="S1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> tokens, which becomes prohibitive for high-resolution meshes containing hundreds of thousands to millions of points.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">A common strategy for reducing attention cost is to introduce a low-dimensional latent bottleneck of size <math id="S1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M\ll N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>≪</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M\ll N</annotation></semantics></math>, reducing complexity to <math id="S1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}(NM)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}(NM)</annotation></semantics></math>.
Low-rank attention methods such as Linformer <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2020</a>)</cite> assume that attention matrices are approximately low-rank and learn explicit <math id="S1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M\times N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M\times N</annotation></semantics></math> projection matrices<span id="S1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span>
While effective at moderate sequence lengths, this approach requires <math id="S1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}(NM)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}(NM)</annotation></semantics></math> parameters per layer and implicitly assumes a fixed token ordering, making it impractical for very long or unordered sequences such as unstructured meshes.
Latent-token architectures such as Perceiver and PerceiverIO <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jaegle et al., 2021b</a>; <a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jaegle et al., 2021a</a>)</cite>, Transolver <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wu et al. (2024)</a></cite>, and Latent Neural Operator (LNO) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang and Wang (2024a)</a></cite> instead use attention projectors to map inputs to a fixed latent array, followed by deep latent-space self-attention.
Notably, most latent-token methods introduce additional transformations inside the latent space, making the overall attention behavior a composition of projections, latent mixing, and nonlinear refinements rather than a single, interpretable operator.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S1.F1" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2508.12594v3/FLARE3.svg" id="S1.F1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:429/225;" width="429" height="225"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S1.F1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 1</span>: </span><span id="S1.F1.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">
<span id="S1.F1.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">FLARE block.</span>
Each head encodes <math id="S1.F1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> input tokens into <math id="S1.F1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> latent tokens with cross-attention <math id="S1.F1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{\mathrm{enc}}=\mathrm{softmax}(Q\cdot K^{T})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>enc</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>softmax</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msup><mi>K</mi><mi>T</mi></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{\mathrm{enc}}=\mathrm{softmax}(Q\cdot K^{T})</annotation></semantics></math> and decodes back with <math id="S1.F1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{\mathrm{dec}}=\mathrm{softmax}(K\cdot Q^{T})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>dec</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>softmax</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msup><mi>Q</mi><mi>T</mi></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{\mathrm{dec}}=\mathrm{softmax}(K\cdot Q^{T})</annotation></semantics></math>, inducing an explicit rank-<math id="S1.F1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\leq M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≤</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\leq M</annotation></semantics></math> input-space mixing operator <math id="S1.F1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W=W_{\mathrm{dec}}\cdot W_{\mathrm{enc}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>W</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>dec</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>enc</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W=W_{\mathrm{dec}}\cdot W_{\mathrm{enc}}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Unlike PerceiverIO <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jaegle et al., 2021a</a>)</cite>, Transolver <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wu et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, and LNO <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang and Wang, 2024a</a>)</cite>, FLARE uses no latent self-attention and executes both steps with fused SDPA kernels <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">Dao et al., 2022</a>)</cite> (see <a href="#A1.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ Appendix A Extended related work ‣ FLARE: Fast Low-rank Attention Routing Engine" class="ltx_ref ltx_refmacro_autoref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure 6</span></a> for a summary).
</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="S1.F2" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2508.12594v3/time_memory_bwd.svg" id="S1.F2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/166;" width="476" height="166"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S1.F2.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 2</span>: </span><span id="S1.F2.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">
Time and memory requirements of different attention schemes.
On an input sequence of one million tokens, FLARE (red) is over <math id="S1.F2.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="200\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>200</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">200\times</annotation></semantics></math> faster than vanilla attention, while consuming marginally more memory.
All models are implemented with FlashAttention <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">Dao et al., 2022</a>)</cite>, and
the memory upper bound on a single H100 80GB GPU is depicted with a dashed line.
Note that the curves for FLARE are somewhat overlapping.
A detailed analysis is presented in <a href="#A7" title="Appendix G Model analysis and ablations ‣ FLARE: Fast Low-rank Attention Routing Engine" class="ltx_ref ltx_refmacro_autoref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix G</span></a>.
</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">We introduce <span id="S1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Fast Low-rank Attention Routing Engine (FLARE)</span>, a token-mixing layer that realizes a <em id="S1.p4.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">flexible low-rank self-attention operator</em> by routing information through a small set of latent tokens.
Concretely, each layer induces an input-input token mixing matrix of rank at most <math id="S1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> via an <em id="S1.p4.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">encode-decode</em> factorization implemented <em id="S1.p4.1.4" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">only</em> with two standard scaled dot-product attention (SDPA) calls; no additional token-mixing is performed.
This formulation makes the induced operator directly analyzable (e.g., via spectra) and keeps the dominant <math id="S1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}(NM)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}(NM)</annotation></semantics></math> computation fully SDPA-compatible, enabling fused attention kernels without materializing <math id="S1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M\times N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M\times N</annotation></semantics></math> projection weights.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">FLARE operationalizes this idea with a minimal architecture: each block performs exactly two cross-attention operations (encode and decode).
Relative to Linformer <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2020</a>)</cite>, FLARE parameterizes low-rank token mixing without learned <math id="S1.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M\times N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M\times N</annotation></semantics></math> projection matrices or a fixed token ordering.
Relative to latent-token architectures such as PerceiverIO <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jaegle et al., 2021a</a>)</cite>, Transolver <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wu et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, and LNO <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang and Wang, 2024a</a>)</cite>, which use latents as a computational workspace and introduce additional latent token mixing, FLARE uses latents only for routing: all token mixing is realized by a single encode-decode factorization on the input tokens, eliminating latent-space self-attention and yielding a mathematically explicit attention operator.
Counterintuitively, we find through systematic ablation that this architectural simplification (removing latent self-attention entirely) consistently improves accuracy while reducing parameters compared to prior latent-attention methods.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">FLARE further assigns disjoint latent slices to each attention head, yielding a mixture of head-specific low-rank operators rather than a single shared bottleneck.
As a result, each head implements an independent low-rank projection–reconstruction pathway, and global communication arises from aggregating multiple such operators.
We analyze these operators using a linear-time eigenanalysis method and observe diverse eigenvalue decay patterns across heads.
A controlled shared-latent ablation collapses these spectra and consistently degrades accuracy, indicating that independent latent routing is an important contributor to expressivity.
Together, these results support the interpretation that FLARE benefits from combining complementary low-rank pathways rather than relying on a single shared projection.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p7.1" class="ltx_p">Taken together, the architectural features of FLARE, (i) explicit encode-decode low-rank factorization, (ii) elimination of latent-space self-attention, and (iii) head-wise independent latent routing, emerge from systematic empirical study as key principles for efficient, scalable attention.
This minimal design enables FLARE to achieve state-of-the-art performance on PDE surrogate benchmarks, scale to one-million-point unstructured meshes on a single GPU, and outperform general-purpose efficient-attention methods, all while using fewer parameters than existing approaches.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p8" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p8.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#S1.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ FLARE: Fast Low-rank Attention Routing Engine" class="ltx_ref ltx_refmacro_autoref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure 1</span></a>illustrates a single FLARE block.
We summarize our main contributions below.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p9" class="ltx_para">
<ul id="S1.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Flexible low-rank attention via latent routing.</span>
We introduce a self-attention formulation in which routing through latent tokens induces an implicit rank-<math id="S1.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\leq M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≤</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\leq M</annotation></semantics></math> attention operator on the input sequence.
FLARE eliminates all latent-space self-attention and expresses attention as a single encode-decode factorization, yielding a mathematically transparent operator.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Head-wise independent low-rank pathways.</span>
By assigning each attention head its own latent slice, FLARE learns a mixture of parallel low-rank operators; targeted ablations show this head-wise independence is critical for accuracy.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Extreme scalability with strong empirical performance.</span>
FLARE trains end-to-end on one-million-point unstructured meshes on a single GPU, achieves state-of-the-art PDE surrogate accuracy, and outperforms efficient-attention baselines on Long Range Arena.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I1.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Benchmark dataset for additive manufacturing.</span>
We release a large-scale thermomechanical additive manufacturing dataset to support research on scalable scientific surrogates.
The dataset is available at <a href="https://huggingface.co/datasets/vedantpuri/LPBF_FLARE" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://huggingface.co/datasets/vedantpuri/LPBF_FLARE</a>.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2 </span>Related work</h2>

<section id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Neural PDE surrogates.</h4>

<div id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Neural operators <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2020</a>; <a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lu et al., 2021</a>; <a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kovachki et al., 2023</a>)</cite> learn mappings between function spaces and enable mesh-independent generalization.
Extensions incorporating geometric priors and graph-based representations improve performance on unstructured meshes <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2023b</a>; <a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2023c</a>)</cite>.
Transformer-based architectures have emerged more recently as powerful PDE surrogates <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">Alkin et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cao, 2021</a>; <a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2022</a>; <a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2023a</a>; <a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hao et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, allowing global context aggregation.
Recent works <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">Alkin et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wu et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">Luo et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang and Wang, 2024a</a>)</cite> leverage latent space attentions for PDE modeling, achieving high accuracy with reduced computational cost.
Building upon these advances, FLARE presents a linear-complexity attention operator tailored to extreme-resolution unstructured domains.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Efficient attention mechanisms.</h4>

<div id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Efficient attention methods reduce cost by constraining attention structure (e.g., rank, sparsity, or locality), yielding restricted subsets of full self-attention with bounded expressivity.
Linformer <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2020</a>)</cite> reduces attention complexity by learning explicit low-rank projections, but requires <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}(NM)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}(NM)</annotation></semantics></math> parameters per layer.
PerceiverIO <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jaegle et al., 2021a</a>)</cite> and related models introduce latent tokens to reduce computational cost, using latent-space self-attention as a computational workspace to aggregate and transform global information.
In this design, interactions between input tokens are mediated through a sequence of latent-space transformations rather than defined by a single, explicit operator on the input tokens.
Transolver <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wu et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">Luo et al., 2025</a>)</cite> and LNO <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang and Wang, 2024a</a>)</cite> adapt this latent projection-unprojection paradigm for PDE surrogate modeling.
FLARE differs from these approaches by using latent tokens solely to induce an explicit low-rank operator, eliminating latent self-attention entirely and enabling a simpler, more analyzable attention formulation.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3 </span>Method</h2>

<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.1 </span>Preliminary: Multi-Head Self-Attention</h3>

<div id="S3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times C}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the input sequence of <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> tokens with <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>C</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math> features each.
The query, key, and value matrices <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q,K,V\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>K</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q,K,V\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times C}</annotation></semantics></math> are obtained by applying learned linear projections to <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S3.E1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q=X\cdot W^{q},\hskip 10.00002ptK=X\cdot W^{k},\hskip 10.00002ptV=X\cdot W^{v}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msup><mi>W</mi><mi>q</mi></msup></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msup><mi>W</mi><mi>k</mi></msup></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msup><mi>W</mi><mi>v</mi></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q=X\cdot W^{q},\hskip 10.00002ptK=X\cdot W^{k},\hskip 10.00002ptV=X\cdot W^{v},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(1)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W^{q},W^{k},W^{v}\in\mathbb{R}^{C\times C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>W</mi><mi>q</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>W</mi><mi>k</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mrow><msup><mi>W</mi><mi>v</mi></msup><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W^{q},W^{k},W^{v}\in\mathbb{R}^{C\times C}</annotation></semantics></math>.
The <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q,\,K,\,V" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mi>K</mi><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mi>V</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q,\,K,\,V</annotation></semantics></math> matrices are then split along the feature dimension and passed to <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>H</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math> heads, each with dimension <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D=C/H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>H</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D=C/H</annotation></semantics></math>, enabling parallel computation of attention:</p>
<table id="S3.E2" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_table">
<tbody>
<tr id="S3.E2X" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E2X.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\left[Q_{1},\ldots,Q_{H}\right]=Q,\,\left[K_{1},\ldots,K_{H}\right]=K,\,\left[V_{1},\ldots,V_{H}\right]=V." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>[</mo><mi>Q</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Q</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>H</mi></msub><mo>]</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mo>[</mo><mi>K</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>K</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>H</mi></msub><mo>]</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>K</mi><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mo>[</mo><mi>V</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>V</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>H</mi></msub><mo>]</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>V</mi><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\left[Q_{1},\ldots,Q_{H}\right]=Q,\,\left[K_{1},\ldots,K_{H}\right]=K,\,\left[V_{1},\ldots,V_{H}\right]=V.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equationgroup ltx_align_right">(2)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">The scaled dot-product attention (SDPA) operation, introduced by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">Vaswani et al., 2017</a>)</cite>, computes the output as</p>
<table id="S3.E3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y_{h}=\text{SDPA}(Q_{h},K_{h},V_{h},s)=\mathrm{softmax}\left(\frac{Q_{h}\cdot K_{h}^{T}}{s}\right)\cdot V_{h}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mtext>SDPA</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>softmax</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msubsup><mi>K</mi><mi>h</mi><mi>T</mi></msubsup></mrow><mi>s</mi></mfrac><mo rspace="0.055em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>h</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y_{h}=\text{SDPA}(Q_{h},K_{h},V_{h},s)=\mathrm{softmax}\left(\frac{Q_{h}\cdot K_{h}^{T}}{s}\right)\cdot V_{h},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(3)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.4" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q_{h},\,K_{h},\,V_{h}\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q_{h},\,K_{h},\,V_{h}\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times D}</annotation></semantics></math> are query, key, and value matrices belonging to head <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math>, and
<math id="S3.SS1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> is typically <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sqrt{D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msqrt><mi>D</mi></msqrt><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{D}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Note that <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{softmax}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>softmax</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{softmax}</annotation></semantics></math> is taken along the row-dimension.
The outputs <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y_{h}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y_{h}</annotation></semantics></math> from all heads are then concatenated along the feature dimension to form the final output</p>
<table id="S3.E4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y=\left[Y_{1},\ldots,Y_{H}\right]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>Y</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>H</mi></msub></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y=\left[Y_{1},\ldots,Y_{H}\right].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(4)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.5" class="ltx_p">This concatenation, followed by a linear layer, enables the model to integrate information across attention heads efficiently.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The greatest cost in multi-head self-attention is the call to SDPA which is <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}(N^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>N</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}(N^{2})</annotation></semantics></math> in time and memory complexity.
This is because <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q_{h}\cdot K_{h}^{T}\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msubsup><mi>K</mi><mi>h</mi><mi>T</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q_{h}\cdot K_{h}^{T}\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times N}</annotation></semantics></math> requires <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}(N^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>N</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}(N^{2})</annotation></semantics></math> storage and softmax, matrix-vector product with <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V_{h}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V_{h}</annotation></semantics></math> takes <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}(N^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>N</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}(N^{2})</annotation></semantics></math> operations.
Fortunately, GPU-optimized multi-head implementations of SDPA are available in PyTorch <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">Paszke, 2019</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.2 </span>FLARE: Fast Low-rank Attention Routing Engine</h3>

<div id="S3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">FLARE is a linear-complexity token mixing layer that learns low-rank global communication structures via attention projections.
The FLARE mechanism introduces a set of <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M\ll N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>≪</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M\ll N</annotation></semantics></math> learnable latent tokens that serve as a bottleneck for information exchange.
The process consists of two stages:</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<ol id="S3.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="S3.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="S3.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Encoding.</span>
The input sequence is projected onto the latent tokens via cross-attention, compressing global information.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S3.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="S3.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Decoding.</span>
The latent tokens are then projected back onto the input sequence, distributing the aggregated information.</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Formally, we define a learnable query matrix <math id="S3.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q\in\mathbb{R}^{M\times C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q\in\mathbb{R}^{M\times C}</annotation></semantics></math>, where each row corresponds to a latent token.
The key and value matrices, <math id="S3.SS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K,V\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>V</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K,V\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times C}</annotation></semantics></math>, are obtained by applying deep residual multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) detailed in <a href="#A2" title="Appendix B Architecture details ‣ FLARE: Fast Low-rank Attention Routing Engine" class="ltx_ref ltx_refmacro_autoref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix B</span></a> to the input <math id="S3.SS2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X</annotation></semantics></math>.
Compared to just a linear layer, these allow the model to learn higher-order feature interactions and deeper nonlinear transformations. Refer to <a href="#A7" title="Appendix G Model analysis and ablations ‣ FLARE: Fast Low-rank Attention Routing Engine" class="ltx_ref ltx_refmacro_autoref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix G</span></a> for ablation studies.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">The matrices <math id="S3.SS2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S3.SS2.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>V</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V</annotation></semantics></math> are first split along the feature dimension into <math id="S3.SS2.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>H</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math> heads, each of dimension <math id="S3.SS2.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D=C/H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>H</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D=C/H</annotation></semantics></math>.
Then, for encoding, each head performs SDPA with a scaling factor <math id="S3.SS2.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s=1</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S3.E5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z_{h}=\mathrm{SDPA}(Q_{h},K_{h},V_{h},s=1)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>Z</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>SDPA</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z_{h}=\mathrm{SDPA}(Q_{h},K_{h},V_{h},s=1).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(5)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.p4.2" class="ltx_p">Here, <math id="S3.SS2.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q_{h}\in\mathbb{R}^{M\times D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q_{h}\in\mathbb{R}^{M\times D}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS2.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K_{h},V_{h}\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K_{h},V_{h}\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times D}</annotation></semantics></math> are query, key, and value matrices belonging to head <math id="S3.SS2.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS2.p4.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z_{h}\in\mathbb{R}^{M\times D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>Z</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z_{h}\in\mathbb{R}^{M\times D}</annotation></semantics></math> is the latent sequence for head <math id="S3.SS2.p4.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math>.
For decoding and propagating information back to the input tokens, we perform a second SDPA operation, swapping the roles of queries and keys and using the latent sequence as values:</p>
<table id="S3.E6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y_{h}=\mathrm{SDPA}(K_{h},Q_{h},Z_{h},s=1)" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>SDPA</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>Z</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y_{h}=\mathrm{SDPA}(K_{h},Q_{h},Z_{h},s=1)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(6)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.p4.3" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS2.p4.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y_{h}\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y_{h}\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times D}</annotation></semantics></math> is the output for each head.
Similar to multi-head self-attention,
the outputs from all heads are concatenated along the feature dimension and passed through a final linear projection to mix information across heads.
As the query matrix has only <math id="S3.SS2.p4.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> tokens, the cost of <span id="S3.SS2.p4.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_markedasmath">SDPA</span> calls in <a href="#S3.E5" title="Equation 5 ‣ 3.2 FLARE: Fast Low-rank Attention Routing Engine ‣ 3 Method ‣ FLARE: Fast Low-rank Attention Routing Engine" class="ltx_ref ltx_refmacro_autoref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Eq. 5</span></a> and <a href="#S3.E6" title="Equation 6 ‣ 3.2 FLARE: Fast Low-rank Attention Routing Engine ‣ 3 Method ‣ FLARE: Fast Low-rank Attention Routing Engine" class="ltx_ref ltx_refmacro_autoref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Eq. 6</span></a> is <math id="S3.SS2.p4.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}(NM)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}(NM)</annotation></semantics></math>.
PyTorch code for the multi-head implementation is presented in <a href="#S3.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 3.2 FLARE: Fast Low-rank Attention Routing Engine ‣ 3 Method ‣ FLARE: Fast Low-rank Attention Routing Engine" class="ltx_ref ltx_refmacro_autoref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure 3</span></a>.
Note that we use a scaling factor <math id="S3.SS2.p4.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s=1</annotation></semantics></math> instead of <math id="S3.SS2.p4.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sqrt{D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msqrt><mi>D</mi></msqrt><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{D}</annotation></semantics></math> in typical transformers <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">Vaswani et al., 2017</a>)</cite> in SDPA.
This modification is explained in <a href="#A7" title="Appendix G Model analysis and ablations ‣ FLARE: Fast Low-rank Attention Routing Engine" class="ltx_ref ltx_refmacro_autoref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix G</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.F3" class="ltx_figure">

<section id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Low-rank communication.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">The two-step attention process can be written as</p>
<table id="S3.E7" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y_{h}=\left(W_{\text{decode},h}\cdot W_{\text{encode},h}\right)\cdot V_{h}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mrow><mtext>decode</mtext><mo>,</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mrow><mtext>encode</mtext><mo>,</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>h</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y_{h}=\left(W_{\text{decode},h}\cdot W_{\text{encode},h}\right)\cdot V_{h}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(7)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">where</p>
<table id="S3.E8" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_table">
<tbody>
<tr id="S3.E8X" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E8X.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle W_{\text{encode},h}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>W</mi><mrow><mtext>encode</mtext><mo>,</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle W_{\text{encode},h}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E8X.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\mathrm{softmax}(Q_{h}\cdot K_{h}^{T})\in\mathbb{R}^{M\times N},\quad\text{and}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>softmax</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msubsup><mi>K</mi><mi>h</mi><mi>T</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mtext>and</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\mathrm{softmax}(Q_{h}\cdot K_{h}^{T})\in\mathbb{R}^{M\times N},\quad\text{and}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="2" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equationgroup ltx_align_right">(8)</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S3.E8Xa" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E8Xa.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle W_{\text{decode},h}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>W</mi><mrow><mtext>decode</mtext><mo>,</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle W_{\text{decode},h}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E8Xa.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\mathrm{softmax}(K_{h}\cdot Q_{h}^{T})\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times M}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>softmax</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msubsup><mi>Q</mi><mi>h</mi><mi>T</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\mathrm{softmax}(K_{h}\cdot Q_{h}^{T})\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times M}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.4" class="ltx_p">Note that <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{softmax}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>softmax</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{softmax}</annotation></semantics></math> is taken along the row-dimension.
We define</p>
<table id="S3.E9" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_table">
<tbody>
<tr id="S3.E9X" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E9X.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle W_{h}=W_{\text{decode},h}\cdot W_{\text{encode},h}\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mrow><mtext>decode</mtext><mo>,</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mrow><mtext>encode</mtext><mo>,</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle W_{h}=W_{\text{decode},h}\cdot W_{\text{encode},h}\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times N}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equationgroup ltx_align_right">(9)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.5" class="ltx_p">as the dense global communication matrix with rank at most <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>.
This low-rank structure, illustrated in <a href="#S1.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ FLARE: Fast Low-rank Attention Routing Engine" class="ltx_ref ltx_refmacro_autoref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure 1</span></a>, enables efficient all-to-all communication without explicitly forming <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{h}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{h}</annotation></semantics></math>; instead, <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{\text{encode},h}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>W</mi><mrow><mtext>encode</mtext><mo>,</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{\text{encode},h}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{\text{decode},h}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>W</mi><mrow><mtext>decode</mtext><mo>,</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{\text{decode},h}</annotation></semantics></math> are applied sequentially, at an overall cost of <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}(MN)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}(MN)</annotation></semantics></math> per head.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.T1" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S3.T1.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 1</span>: </span><span id="S3.T1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">
(Top) relative <math id="S3.T1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> error (<math id="S3.T1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times 10^{-3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times 10^{-3}</annotation></semantics></math>) and (bottom) parameter count for different models across PDE benchmark problems.
The best results (smallest error) are made bold, and the second best results are underlined.
A backslash (<math id="S3.T1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\backslash" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>\</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\backslash</annotation></semantics></math>) indicates that the model cannot be applied to the benchmark,
and tilde (<math id="S3.T1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∼</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim</annotation></semantics></math>) indicates that the model is prohibitively slow on the benchmark.

</section>
<section id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Discussion on the design principles of FLARE.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">FLARE’s latent tokens implement a structured gather-scatter communication pattern: encoding pools input values into <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> compact global descriptors, then decoding selectively broadcasts these back along the same pathways, yielding a low-rank routing operator that avoids explicit all-to-all interactions.
This mechanism relies on two design choices discussed in <a href="#A6" title="Appendix F Discussion on the design principles of FLARE. ‣ FLARE: Fast Low-rank Attention Routing Engine" class="ltx_ref ltx_refmacro_autoref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix F</span></a>: (i) symmetric encode-decode operators promote stable information flow without redundant parameters, and (ii) fixed input-independent latent queries simplify the low-rank structure and improve efficiency, shifting expressive capacity to deep residual key/value projections that recover representational power.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">FLARE block.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#S1.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ FLARE: Fast Low-rank Attention Routing Engine" class="ltx_ref ltx_refmacro_autoref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure 1</span></a> (left) illustrates a single FLARE block.
Given input tokens <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times C}</annotation></semantics></math>, the output of an FLARE block is computed as</p>
<table id="S3.E10" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_table">
<tbody>
<tr id="S3.E10X" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E10X.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle X</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E10X.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=X+\text{FLARE}\left(\text{LayerNorm}\left(X\right)\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mtext>FLARE</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mtext>LayerNorm</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=X+\text{FLARE}\left(\text{LayerNorm}\left(X\right)\right)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="2" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equationgroup ltx_align_right">(10)</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S3.E10Xa" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E10Xa.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle X</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E10Xa.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=X+\text{ResMLP}\left(\text{LayerNorm}\left(X\right)\right)." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mtext>ResMLP</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mtext>LayerNorm</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=X+\text{ResMLP}\left(\text{LayerNorm}\left(X\right)\right).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Here, <span id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_markedasmath">ResMLP</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">He et al., 2016</a>)</cite> denotes a residual MLP block detailed in <a href="#A2" title="Appendix B Architecture details ‣ FLARE: Fast Low-rank Attention Routing Engine" class="ltx_ref ltx_refmacro_autoref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix B</span></a>, and <span id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_markedasmath">LayerNorm</span> denotes layer normalization <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ba et al., 2016</a>)</cite> operation.
To summarize, a FLARE block consists of a token mixing operation via FLARE, a pointwise residual MLP, and layer normalization in pre-norm format <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xiong et al., 2020</a>)</cite>.
Deep residual MLPs within the block enable complex, token-level feature transformations and improve accuracy.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Overall design.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The overall architecture is given by <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math> sequential FLARE blocks sandwiched between an input projection and an output projection, which are detailed in <a href="#A2" title="Appendix B Architecture details ‣ FLARE: Fast Low-rank Attention Routing Engine" class="ltx_ref ltx_refmacro_autoref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix B</span></a>.
Such a design enables the model to efficiently integrate local and global information across multiple layers, making it well suited for large-scale, high-dimensional data such as point clouds.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.F4" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
