<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(25)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A8.SS1.p3.2" class="ltx_p">layer-by-layer within a finite element framework
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">Denlinger et al., 2014</a>; <a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liang et al., 2019</a>; <a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">Autodesk, 2025</a>)</cite>, and are integrated in commercial software products <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">Autodesk, 2025</a>)</cite>.
These calculations take several minutes to hours, making them prohibitively expensive for part design scenarios that can involve hundreds of evaluations.</p>
</div>
<div id="A8.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ferguson et al. (2025)</a></cite> introduced a dataset of LPBF simulations in which multiple finite element calculations were performed on a collection of 3D shapes.
That dataset, however, was restricted to relatively coarse meshes with approximately 3,500 points per mesh.
The present work extends this line of research by considering larger and more refined meshes, with up to 50,000 grid points.</p>
</div>

</figure>

Qualitative results for FLARE on the LPBF <math id="A8.F16.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z</annotation></semantics></math>-displacement prediction task.
For each test geometry,
we show the ground truth <math id="A8.F16.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z</annotation></semantics></math>-displacement field, the model prediction, and the corresponding error (Ground Truth <math id="A8.F16.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math> Prediction).
</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">H.2 </span>Dataset Generation</h3>

<div id="A8.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To generate a dataset of LPBF simulations, we employ Autodesk NetFabb <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">Autodesk, 2025</a>)</cite>, a commercially available software tool for numerically simulating RS and associated physics.
We begin with the Fusion 360 segmentation dataset <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lambourne et al., 2021</a>)</cite>, and scale each shape to lie within
<math id="A8.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[-30,30]\times[-30,30]\times[0,60]~\text{mm}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>30</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>30</mn></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>30</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>30</mn></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>60</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.330em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>mm</mtext></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[-30,30]\times[-30,30]\times[0,60]~\text{mm}</annotation></semantics></math>
such that it rests atop the build plate at <math id="A8.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z\in[-25,0]~\text{mm}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>25</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.330em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>mm</mtext></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z\in[-25,0]~\text{mm}</annotation></semantics></math>; the parts are not otherwise rotated or transformed.
The simulation is then carried out for the
Renishaw AM250 machine
and <span id="A8.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Ti-6Al-4V</span> material system deposited with
<math id="A8.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="40~\mu\text{m}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>40</mn><mo lspace="0.330em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>μ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>m</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">40~\mu\text{m}</annotation></semantics></math> thickness.
Other parameters are left as their default nominal values and no support structures are added <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ferguson et al., 2025</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A8.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">In AM, the material is deposited layer by layer, and ideally, a high-fidelity simulation would model each layer individually.
However, this can be computationally expensive, especially for builds with hundreds or thousands of layers.
Layer lumping simplifies this process by combining multiple physical layers into a single <em id="A8.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">lumped</em> computational layer.
In our calculations, NetFabb applies layer-lumping with a lumped layer thickness of <math id="A8.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.5~\text{mm}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2.5</mn><mo lspace="0.330em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>mm</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.5~\text{mm}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A8.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">NetFabb re-meshes the geometry to contain axis-aligned hexahedral elements before simulating the build process.
Then, NetFabb generates a thermal and a mechanical history for each part
corresponding to lumped layer deposition steps during the build.
We obtain the displacement, elastic strain, von Mises stress, and temperature fields evaluated at all nodal locations throughout the build.
NetFabb also provides field values after the part has cooled down and detached from the build plate.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">H.3 </span>Benchmark task</h3>

<div id="A8.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To evaluate neural surrogate models, we target a field prediction task that is both central to our dataset and broadly relevant to the AM community: predicting residual vertical (<math id="A8.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z</annotation></semantics></math>) displacement.
In LPBF, each layer is fused by a laser and followed by a recoater blade that spreads powder uniformly across the build area <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Reijonen et al., 2024</a>)</cite>.
Overhanging features may cause vertical displacements that interfere with the blade’s path, potentially leading to collisions. Predicting the <math id="A8.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z</annotation></semantics></math>-displacement field can therefore help identify risk of blade collision failures.
Rapid estimation of displacement prior to a build, thus, is highly desirable for design troubleshooting, as severe distortion can render a part unusable.
Moreover, accurate prediction of nodal displacements can help anticipate build failures <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ferguson et al., 2025</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A8.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Since full-scale LPBF simulations are computationally expensive—taking minutes to hours—a fast surrogate model offers a valuable alternative for accelerating AM design.
Accordingly, we train our models to predict the <math id="A8.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z</annotation></semantics></math>-displacement at every node at the final time step.</p>
</div>
<div id="A8.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">More formally,
the input to a neural surrogate model is the volumetric axis-aligned hexahedral mesh describing the geometry.
This includes the point-coordinates (array of size <math id="A8.SS3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N\times 3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\times 3</annotation></semantics></math> where <math id="A8.SS3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> is the number of points) and, optionally, mesh connectivity information.
The corresponding label is the <math id="A8.SS3.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z</annotation></semantics></math> displacement value at each point (array of size <math id="A8.SS3.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N\times 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\times 1</annotation></semantics></math>).</p>
</div>
<div id="A8.SS3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS3.p4.1" class="ltx_p">While this dataset focuses on a steady-state prediction problem, future iterations of this benchmark could involve learning dynamic surrogate models that track the time-history of stress and deformation fields during the build process.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">H.4 </span>Data filtering</h3>

<div id="A8.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The dataset contains a wide-ranging set of shapes, making the dataset general enough to train a strong data-driven field prediction model.
Out of <math id="A8.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∼</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim</annotation></semantics></math>27,000 shapes, 19,732 were successfully simulated.
We analyze the first 3,500 successful simulations and filter them according to several statistics to design a balanced training and test set.
For example, we limit the learning problem to meshes with up to 50,000 points and up to 300,000 edges.
This is done to reduce memory usage which becomes a bottleneck when training on small GPUs.
We also filter meshes that have high aspect ratio elements as the FEM calculation could be unreliable on highly distorted geometries.
Our dataset processing code is available in the GitHub repository associated with this paper.
The statistics for the filtered dataset are presented in <a href="#A8.T6" title="Table 6 ‣ H.1 Introduction &amp; Background ‣ Appendix H Benchmark dataset of additive manufacturing simulations ‣ FLARE: Fast Low-rank Attention Routing Engine" class="ltx_ref ltx_refmacro_autoref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table 6</span></a> along with histograms in <a href="#A8.F15" title="Figure 15 ‣ H.1 Introduction &amp; Background ‣ Appendix H Benchmark dataset of additive manufacturing simulations ‣ FLARE: Fast Low-rank Attention Routing Engine" class="ltx_ref ltx_refmacro_autoref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure 15</span></a>.
A gallery of successful simulations is presented in <a href="#A8.F14" title="Figure 14 ‣ Appendix H Benchmark dataset of additive manufacturing simulations ‣ FLARE: Fast Low-rank Attention Routing Engine" class="ltx_ref ltx_refmacro_autoref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure 14</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">H.5 </span>Qualitative Results for LPBF <math id="A8.SS5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z</annotation></semantics></math>-Displacement Prediction</h3>

<div id="A8.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In <a href="#A8.F16" title="Figure 16 ‣ H.1 Introduction &amp; Background ‣ Appendix H Benchmark dataset of additive manufacturing simulations ‣ FLARE: Fast Low-rank Attention Routing Engine" class="ltx_ref ltx_refmacro_autoref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure 16</span></a>, we present visualizations of ground-truth <math id="A8.SS5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z</annotation></semantics></math>-displacement, predictions by FLARE, and the corresponding error.
Across a set of representative geometries from the LPBF test set, FLARE produces displacement fields that are visually indistinguishable from the ground truth and capture both the global deformation patterns and localized high-gradient regions.
Importantly, the error fields remain low-magnitude and spatially diffuse, with no systematic accumulation near edges or corners—indicating that the model does not rely on positional shortcuts or overfit to particular geometric artifacts.
This suggests that FLARE successfully learns the dominant thermo-mechanical modes of deformation while only missing small higher-order variations that are difficult to resolve without substantially larger latent bottlenecks.
These qualitative observations are consistent with the low average relative <math id="A8.SS5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>L</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> error and illustrate that FLARE maintains stable accuracy across a diverse distribution of part geometries.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">H.6 </span>Dataset split and benchmark protocol</h3>

<section id="A8.SS6.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Splits.</h4>

<div id="A8.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">From the full set of 19,732 successful LPBF simulations, we construct a filtered subset of cases with up to 50,000 points per geometry.
We use 1,100 cases for training and 290 cases for testing, as summarized in <a href="#A4.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ D.1 Benchmark metrics ‣ Appendix D Benchmarking and Comparison ‣ FLARE: Fast Low-rank Attention Routing Engine" class="ltx_ref ltx_refmacro_autoref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table 3</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS6.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Inputs and outputs.</h4>

<div id="A8.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For each case, the benchmark input consists of the 3D mesh node coordinates <math id="A8.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times 3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times 3}</annotation></semantics></math>.
The benchmark target is the final-time-step vertical displacement field (<math id="A8.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z</annotation></semantics></math>-displacement) <math id="A8.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times 1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times 1}</annotation></semantics></math> at the same nodes.
We focus on this scalar displacement because it is directly tied to recoater-blade interference risk in LPBF.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS6.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Simulation context.</h4>

<div id="A8.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">All parts are scaled to lie within a standardized build volume <math id="A8.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[-30,30]\times[-30,30]\times[0,60]~\text{mm}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>30</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>30</mn></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>30</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>30</mn></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>60</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.330em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>mm</mtext></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[-30,30]\times[-30,30]\times[0,60]~\text{mm}</annotation></semantics></math> and simulated in Autodesk NetFabb for the Renishaw AM250 machine and Ti-6Al-4V material system, using <math id="A8.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="40~\mu\text{m}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>40</mn><mo lspace="0.330em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>μ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>m</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">40~\mu\text{m}</annotation></semantics></math> layer thickness and layer lumping with a lumped layer height of <math id="A8.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.5~\text{mm}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2.5</mn><mo lspace="0.330em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>mm</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.5~\text{mm}</annotation></semantics></math>.
These settings follow the procedure described in <a href="#A8" title="Appendix H Benchmark dataset of additive manufacturing simulations ‣ FLARE: Fast Low-rank Attention Routing Engine" class="ltx_ref ltx_refmacro_autoref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix H</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>

    target="_blank" rel="nofollow">view the build logs</a>
    for errors. Generated by
    <a href="https://math.nist.gov/~BMiller/LaTeXML/" target="_blank" class="ltx_ref ltx_LaTeXML_logo">
      <span style="letter-spacing: -0.2em; margin-right: 0.1em;">
        L
        <span style="font-size: 70%; position: relative; bottom: 2.2pt;">A</span>
        T
        <span style="position: relative; bottom: -0.4ex;">E</span>
      </span>
      <span class="ltx_font_smallcaps">xml</span>
      <img alt="[LOGO]"
        src="data:image/png;base64,">
    </a>.
  </div>
  <div class="keyboard-glossary">
    <h2>Instructions for reporting errors</h2>
    <p>We are continuing to improve HTML versions of papers, and your feedback helps enhance accessibility and mobile
      support. To report errors in the HTML that will help us improve conversion and rendering, choose any of the
      methods listed below:</p>
    <ul>
      <li>Click the "Report Issue" <span class="mobile-only">(<svg role="presentation"
            style="display: inline-block; vertical-align: middle; fill: var(--text-color);" aria-hidden="true"
            height="1em" viewBox="0 0 640 640">
            <path
              d="M224 160C224 107 267 64 320 64C373 64 416 107 416 160L416 163.6C416 179.3 403.3 192 387.6 192L252.5 192C236.8 192 224.1 179.3 224.1 163.6L224.1 160zM569.6 172.8C580.2 186.9 577.3 207 563.2 217.6L465.4 290.9C470.7 299.8 474.7 309.6 477.2 320L576 320C593.7 320 608 334.3 608 352C608 369.7 593.7 384 576 384L480 384L480 416C480 418.6 479.9 421.3 479.8 423.9L563.2 486.4C577.3 497 580.2 517.1 569.6 531.2C559 545.3 538.9 548.2 524.8 537.6L461.7 490.3C438.5 534.5 395.2 566.5 344 574.2L344 344C344 330.7 333.3 320 320 320C306.7 320 296 330.7 296 344L296 574.2C244.8 566.5 201.5 534.5 178.3 490.3L115.2 537.6C101.1 548.2 81 545.3 70.4 531.2C59.8 517.1 62.7 497 76.8 486.4L160.2 423.9C160.1 421.3 160 418.7 160 416L160 384L64 384C46.3 384 32 369.7 32 352C32 334.3 46.3 320 64 320L162.8 320C165.3 309.6 169.3 299.8 174.6 290.9L76.8 217.6C62.7 207 59.8 186.9 70.4 172.8C81 158.7 101.1 155.8 115.2 166.4L224 248C236.3 242.9 249.8 240 264 240L376 240C390.2 240 403.7 242.8 416 248L524.8 166.4C538.9 155.8 559 158.7 569.6 172.8z" />
          </svg>)</span> button, located in the page header.</li>
    </ul>
    <p><strong>Tip:</strong> You can select the relevant text first, to include it in your report.</p>
    <p>Our team has already identified <a class="ltx_ref" href="https://github.com/arXiv/html_feedback/issues"
        target="_blank">the following issues</a>. We appreciate your time reviewing and reporting rendering errors we
      may not have found yet. Your efforts will help us improve the HTML versions for all readers, because disability
      should not be a barrier to accessing research. Thank you for your continued support in championing open access for
      all.</p>
    <p>Have a free development cycle? Help support accessibility at arXiv! Our collaborators at LaTeXML maintain a <a
        class="ltx_ref" href="https://github.com/brucemiller/LaTeXML/wiki/Porting-LaTeX-packages-for-LaTeXML"
        target="_blank">list of packages that need conversion</a>, and welcome <a class="ltx_ref"
        href="https://github.com/brucemiller/LaTeXML/issues" target="_blank">developer contributions</a>.</p>
  </div>
